title: Anticoncentration for low degree
statement: Let $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$ be a real-valued function on the uniform Boolean cube, and let $k\in\mathbb N$. Suppose every nonzero Fourier coefficient of $f$ is supported on a set of size at most $k$, and that $\operatorname{Var}(f)>0$. Then $\dfrac{9}{16\cdot 9^k}\le \Pr\!\left(\dfrac{\sqrt{\operatorname{Var}(f)}}{2}<|f-\E f|\right)$.
replaced: Let $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$ be a function on the uniform Boolean cube of Fourier degree at most $k\in\mathbb N$ with variance $V>0$. Then $9/(16\cdot9^k)\le\Pr(|f-\mathbb Ef|>\sqrt V/2)$.
